deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematical derivation. It is a heavily corrected German prose draft by Riemann describing his own scientific work and its intellectual sources, of the kind written for a CV, an application or a 'Selbstanzeige'. A cleaned version of its final passages was printed by Dedekind and Weber in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke, at the head of the 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts'. The surviving layers of the draft are as follows.

(1) First attempt (top, partly struck). A study of the connection between light, magnetism and electricity (the word 'Wärme' is struck here) requires a different conception of the known laws of nature, that is, their expression through other fundamental concepts. Next to this is a marginal addition: 'und eine Anknüpfung an die Psychologie Herbarts'.

(2) Second attempt. 'Eine neue Auffassung der bekannten Naturgesetze (Ausdruck derselben mittelst anderer Grundbegriffe)' made it possible to use the experimental data on the interaction ('Wechselwirkung') between heat/light, magnetism and electricity to investigate their connection. 'Ich wurde dazu hauptsächlich durch das Studium der Werke Newton's, Euler's und — andererseits — Herbart's geführt.' This sentence is struck or reworked on the page. Further words appear below it: 'wissenschaftlichen Arbeiten' and a name read as 'Cartesius' (uncertain); see transcription corrections.

(3) Mathematical work (several struck attempts, then a cleaner one). Item 1 is the introduction of the imaginary into the theory of other transcendental functions, as already done for algebraic functions. The reference given is 'Vgl. meine Dissertation Art. 20', the 1851 dissertation's closing programmatic article. Riemann says he supplied the necessary general preliminary work for this. Item 2 is his method for integrating partial differential equations. He says he has already applied it successfully to physical problems in the theory of electricity and of elasticity. A struck parenthesis seems to name a specific elasticity topic ('...schen Klangfiguren/Schwingungen', perhaps Chladni figures). The electricity work presumably points to his 1855 paper on Nobili's colour rings. An item '3)' is begun but left empty.

(4) Bottom passage, which corresponds to the text printed in the Werke. As regards Herbart, Riemann could almost entirely adopt Herbart's earliest investigations. Their results were stated in Herbart's doctoral and habilitation theses ('vom 22. u. 23. Oct. 1802'). He had, however, to depart from the later course of Herbart's speculation in one essential point. This produces a difference regarding Herbart's philosophy of nature and those propositions of psychology that concern its connection with the philosophy of nature (the last clause is only partly legible).

There is nothing to compute. The 'problem served' is biographical self-presentation: the unified field-theoretic programme (light, heat, magnetism, electricity), complex-function theory per Dissertation Art. 20, and PDE methods with applications.
errors: No mathematical errors are possible since there is no mathematics. Historically, the date 22–23 Oct. 1802 for Herbart's Göttingen promotion/habilitation disputations is correct. The draft's inconsistent numbering (1), 1), 2), 2), 3)) and its struck alternatives are draft artefacts, not errors.

results.what: Self-description of the research programme: a new conception of the laws of nature via other fundamental concepts, used to unify light, heat, magnetism and electricity; sources named as Newton, Euler and Herbart.
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann himself; the cleaned text is printed in Werke, 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts'

results.what: Reference to extending complex methods from algebraic to other transcendental functions (Dissertation Art. 20), and to his PDE integration method applied to electricity (Nobili rings, 1855) and elasticity.
results.modern_name: Riemann's complex-analytic programme; Riemann's method for PDEs

results.what: Statement of agreement with Herbart's earliest work (theses of Oct. 1802) and divergence from his later speculation.
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (well known from the Werke and Scholz's studies of Riemann and Herbart)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the draft of a well-known published autobiographical statement (Werke, philosophical fragments) and is much discussed in the literature on Riemann and Herbart. Only the intermediate draft variants, such as the explicit crossing out of 'Wärme' and the Klangfiguren remark, add minor detail.
transcription_corrections: Bottom passage, which the machine transcription garbles. It should read approximately: 'Was letzteren betrifft, so konnte ich mich den frühesten Untersuchungen Herbarts, deren Resultate in seiner Promotions- u. Habilitationsschrift (vom 22. u. 23. Oct. 1802) ausgesprochen sind, fast völlig anschliessen, musste aber von dem späteren Gange seiner Speculation in einem wesentlichen Punkte abweichen, wodurch eine Verschiedenheit in Bezug auf seine Naturphilosophie und diejenigen Sätze der Psychologie, welche deren Verbindung mit der Naturphilosophie betreffen, bedingt ist.'
'Die ersten Vorträge (Vorlesungen)' should be 'Was letzteren betrifft ... frühesten Untersuchungen Herbarts'.
'kann völlig unterschreiben' should be 'fast völlig anschliessen'.
'späteren Aussage ... Speculation' should be 'späteren Gange seiner Speculation'.

Second attempt: read 'wodurch die Benutzung der experimentellen data ... möglich wurde' rather than '[-erschien-] mir ... möglich zu werden'. The printed version reads 'Wärme, Licht, Magnetismus und Electricität'.
'Cartesius [?]' is doubtful. It is more likely part of the phrase '— andererseits — Herbart's' or a stray reworking; the image does not clearly support 'Cartesius'.
The parenthesis in item 2 appears to contain '...schen Klangfiguren' (possibly 'Chladni'schen'), not '...schen Schwingungen'.
